note: Concern taxonomy used by the dialogue manager and the natural-language detector. Keywords are evidence, not diagnoses. A single weak keyword never triggers a recommendation on its own.

concerns.label: Sadness or low mood
concerns.description: Feeling down, tearful, empty or low.
empathy: That sounds heavy. Thank you for saying it out loud.
Sadness can make everything feel slower, and it makes sense that it is on your mind.
concerns.normalise: You do not have to justify feeling low or prove that it is 'bad enough'.
concerns.risk_note: If low mood has lasted more than two weeks or is affecting daily life, a professional conversation is worth considering.

concerns.label: Loneliness or isolation
concerns.description: Feeling alone, left out, or without someone to talk to.
empathy: Feeling alone can hurt even when there are people physically nearby.
It sounds like you have been carrying this without much company.
concerns.normalise: Needing connection is human, not needy.

concerns.label: Stress or pressure
concerns.description: Feeling under pressure, stretched thin, or unable to switch off.
empathy: That is a lot to hold at once. No wonder you feel stretched.
Pressure that does not let up is exhausting, even when you look fine from outside.
concerns.normalise: Struggling under pressure is not a sign of weakness.

concerns.label: Anxiety or worry
concerns.description: Worry, nervousness, racing thoughts or a sense of dread.
empathy: Anxiety can make the mind run fast even when you want it to rest.
That sounds uncomfortable and tiring. Thank you for telling me.
concerns.normalise: Worry is not a character flaw, and you are not 'too much' for feeling it.

concerns.label: Panic or sudden fear
concerns.description: Sudden intense fear, a racing heart, or feeling unable to breathe.
empathy: Panic can feel frightening in your body. I am glad you are here talking about it.
That sounds intense, and it makes sense that it has stayed with you.
concerns.normalise: Panic sensations are real and distressing, even when there is no obvious danger.
concerns.risk_note: If you have chest pain, faintness or trouble breathing for the first time, seek medical care. Panic and physical health problems can look alike.

concerns.label: Low motivation
concerns.description: Difficulty starting things, low energy, or feeling apathetic.
empathy: Starting anything can feel enormous when motivation is low.
That stuck feeling is real, and it does not mean you are lazy.
concerns.normalise: Low motivation is often a sign you are depleted, not a moral failure.

concerns.label: Sleep difficulties
concerns.description: Trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling unrested.
empathy: Sleep problems make everything else harder to carry.
Not being able to rest when you need to is genuinely frustrating.
concerns.normalise: Sleep and mood affect each other; struggling with sleep is common and treatable.
concerns.risk_note: If sleep problems continue for several weeks, or you feel sleepy while driving, speak to a doctor.

concerns.label: Harsh self-talk
concerns.description: Self-criticism, guilt, shame, or a strong sense of not being good enough.
empathy: That inner voice sounds very harsh. You do not deserve to be spoken to that way.
Carrying that much self-blame is tiring.
concerns.normalise: A critical inner voice is common, and it can be challenged gently.

concerns.label: Anger or frustration
concerns.description: Irritation, rage, or frustration that feels hard to contain.
empathy: Anger can be a signal that something matters to you, or that a boundary has been crossed.
That frustration sounds like it has been building up.
concerns.normalise: Anger is not automatically bad; what matters is what you can do with it safely.
concerns.risk_note: If you feel you might hurt yourself or someone else, move away and contact emergency services or a trusted person.

concerns.label: Feeling overwhelmed
concerns.description: Too many demands at once, or feeling unable to cope with the pile.
empathy: When everything arrives at once, it makes sense that your system feels flooded.
That sounds like far more than one person should have to juggle.
concerns.normalise: Overwhelm is a signal about load, not a verdict on your ability.

concerns.label: Grief or loss
concerns.description: Sadness after a death, breakup, or significant loss.
empathy: I am sorry for your loss. Grief can arrive in waves, and there is no correct timeline.
That kind of absence can shape ordinary days in unexpected ways.
concerns.normalise: Grief is not a problem to solve quickly. It is something to make room for.
concerns.risk_note: If grief makes it hard to care for yourself or lasts a long time without easing, professional support can help.

concerns.label: Study or work pressure
concerns.description: Exams, deadlines, grades, job pressure or placement stress.
empathy: Study pressure can take over your whole sense of self if it is not contained.
That sounds like a lot of pressure, especially if the stakes feel high.
concerns.normalise: Your worth is not your marks or your output.

concerns.label: Emotional exhaustion
concerns.description: Feeling drained, detached, or running on empty for a long time.
empathy: That sounds like exhaustion that rest has not fixed. It makes sense that you are running low.
Carrying this for a long time takes a real toll.
concerns.normalise: Burnout is a response to prolonged load, not a lack of resilience.
concerns.risk_note: If you are unable to function at work, study or home, consider speaking to a doctor or counsellor.

concerns.label: Relationship difficulty
concerns.description: Conflict, breakup, family tension or difficulty with someone close.
empathy: Relationship pain can sit right at the centre of the day.
That sounds like a difficult thing to carry, especially when the person matters to you.
concerns.normalise: Conflict and distance in close relationships are painful, and needing support with them is normal.

concerns.label: Social anxiety
concerns.description: Fear of judgement, embarrassment, or social situations.
empathy: Being watched or judged can feel intensely uncomfortable, even when others do not notice.
That kind of fear can make ordinary interactions feel like a test.
concerns.normalise: Social anxiety is common, and it responds to gradual, supported steps.

duration.question: How long has this been weighing on you?
duration.help: There is no wrong answer. This helps me choose gentler suggestions.

options.label: As long as I can remember

impact.question: How much is it affecting your daily life?
impact.help: This is about how it feels to you, not a score.

sleep_hours.question: Roughly how many hours are you sleeping on a usual night?

support.question: Do you have anyone you can talk to about this?
support.help: This helps me avoid suggesting something that does not fit your situation.

energy.question: How is your energy right now?
energy.help: Suggestions will be sized to what feels possible.
